chunks: "Whoever says, when he hears the adhan of al-subh: O Allah, I ask You by the coming of Your day, the departing of Your night, the presence of Your prayers, and the voices of Your callers, that You turn to me in repentance,
Indeed, You are the Oft-Returning in mercy, the Merciful.

and says the like of that when he hears the adhan of al-maghrib, then dies during his day or his night, he dies repentant. And Ibn al-Nabbah used to say in his adhan: Hayya 'ala khayr al-'amal, hayya 'ala khayr al-'amal. So whenever Ali عليه السلام saw him, he would say:
"Welcome to those who speak justly, and welcome and greetings to the prayer."

key_terms.التَّوَّابُ: the One who repeatedly accepts repentance
key_terms.تَتُوبَ: to accept repentance and turn mercifully toward the servant
key_terms.حَيَّ عَلَى خَيْرِ الْعَمَلِ: hasten to the best of deeds

ai.seo_question: What should be said when hearing the adhan of Fajr and Maghrib for repentance?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a supplication to be recited when hearing the adhan of Fajr and similarly at Maghrib, seeking tawbah from Allah. It promises that one who recites it and dies that day or night dies in a state of repentance, and it also preserves a report about the adhan phrase "Hayya 'ala khayr al-'amal" and Imam Ali's عليه السلام approval of it.
